7	## 2026-08-05 — Quiz copy acted on the 29 July feedback session
8	
9	**Why.** Mark walked the quiz through a live critique on 29 July. Most of it was
10	acted on within a day (email capture back at the end, the role question, the
11	question copy pass), but six items were still outstanding a week later. This is
12	those six.
13	
14	**The results heading was the largest one.** `heading: 'Here's what I see'` was
15	the H1 on the results page and said nothing about the person reading it, while
16	the sentence that _did_ ("Most of your last few Sprints went to the mechanical
17	work") sat two blocks below as the shape's `mostLine`. The specific sentence was
18	in the wrong place, so it swapped up into the heading: `mapMove.heading` now takes
19	the same `{box}` substitution `mostLine` already had, and `scrum-master-ai` drops
20	`mostLine` rather than printing the same sentence twice. The first thing on the
21	page is now about the taker instead of about the page. `mostlyTop` / `mostlyBottom`
22	stay as the reading line under the shape, still suppressed when the largest box
23	already sits on the majority row. `headingFallback` covers the case where the
24	heading wants a `{box}` and no shape was computed; for this quiz that needs every
25	answered option to lack a `box`, so it is a guard rather than a path anyone hits.
26	
27	**"About your situation" is now "the constraints you described".** Naming what
28	the strip actually contains rather than gesturing at it. One option sits oddly
29	under that heading, q8's "I coach through the work as I go", which is a
30	legitimate way to work and not a constraint; that is one option in thirty-two and
31	was accepted rather than reworded.
32	
33	**The page now points forward at the payoff.** The critique was that the single
34	most valuable block sits last with nothing above leading up to it. Two changes,
35	no reorder: `opening` ends by saying what is coming ("Below: where your Sprints
36	actually went, then the one change I'd make first"), and the shape's move tags
37	went from `less of this` / `more of this` to `take time from here` / `put it
38	here`, which is the same language the move block itself uses. Worth knowing that
39	the long tag can only ever land on the mechanical box: `reclaimPriority` is
40	q3/q1/q2 and every eligible answer in those three is `box: mechanical`, which is
41	the full-width bottom row. The short tag is the one that lands on a half-width
42	top-row box.
43	
44	**Three question stems were still too long** (q5 at 146 characters, q7 at 190, q8
45	at 140). The 30 July copy pass fixed tone, not length. Trimming these is safe for
46	the reason recorded in that entry: question and answer text are read together, so
47	a phrase in the stem that the options already carry is dead weight, which is the
48	opposite of the rule for result sentences. q5 lost the list its options already
49	name, q7 kept a shortened list because "better at their own job" is undefined
50	without one, and q8 lost "the way they work together", which overlapped q4.
51	
52	**"Get one thing to try" became "focus on".** "Try" reads as "maybe this will
53	work, maybe it won't", which undersells the one block the whole page is built
54	around.
55	
56	**Two defects fixed in passing:** `close` read "GenAI will not magically you or
57	your team more productive", and `slippingEmpty` had no full stop.
58	
59	**Still outstanding from the same session, deliberately.** Role-conditional
60	result copy (the role tag reaches Cakemail and drives the manager `lens`, but
61	nothing on the results page varies by it) and a pain-led hero kicker. Both need
62	copy only Mark can write, and the role one needs a decision about how far to take
63	it: the critique proposed roles × result buckets, which is a 4× multiplier on
64	copy maintained by one person.
65	
66	## 2026-08-04 — Course dates come from Corsizio, not from four hand-typed copies
67	
68	**Why.** Course dates lived in four places: the `workshops` array in each course
69	page's frontmatter, `email-automation/newsletters/courses.json` for the
70	newsletter, the `date` in each `email-automation/courses/*.json` cohort config,
71	and the AI Tsunami page's prose. Three of the four were wrong on the day this was
72	written. The CSPO and CSD-technical pages were still advertising June classes
73	that had already run. `csm-virtual.json` said June 15 while the site sold
74	September 3. And `newsletters/courses.json` listed a July 28 CSM whose Corsizio
75	event returned 404 in every status: the course was cancelled after the newsletter
76	went out, so subscribers were sent a dead "Register" link. Nothing was broken in
77	a way anything would report; four copies of a fact simply drift.
78	
79	**What it is now.** Corsizio is the source of truth. `npm run sync-courses`
80	writes `shared/course-schedule.json`, and the course pages, the "Get Certified"
81	tabs, the JSON-LD and the newsletter all read it. The cohort configs keep only
82	what Corsizio has never heard of (Zoom, Mural, docs folders) plus a
83	`corsizioEventId`; their dates resolve live. So it is two and a half places
84	collapsed into one, the half being the cohort config, which had to keep its own
85	file because no calendar system knows our Mural board.
86	
87	**Why the file is committed rather than fetched at build.** A build-time fetch
88	would let a Corsizio outage break a deploy, and would _still_ need scheduled
89	builds to notice a newly-scheduled course, so it buys fragility without escaping
90	staleness. Committed in `shared/`, pushing it triggers the rebuild by itself and
91	git records every schedule change.
92	
93	**Why the email path fetches live anyway.** The generated file holds only future
94	events, but the post-course email is sent _after_ the class, when the cohort's
95	event is no longer in it. So `resolveCourseConfig()` does a by-id lookup, which
96	Corsizio answers for past events. Two mechanisms, because they answer different
97	questions: "what is on sale" versus "what was this cohort". A deleted event 404s
98	and throws rather than falling back to a stale local date, so the cancelled-course
99	case that produced the dead newsletter link now stops a send instead.
100	
101	**Mapping is by category id, not event name.** Every Corsizio event carries
102	exactly one category and the ids are stable, so retitling a workshop cannot break
103	the mapping; matching on names would have. Two things fell out of the probe worth
104	recording: `startDate`/`endDate` are UTC instants with a separate `timeZone`, so
105	every label and day count is computed in the event's zone or a 9am Toronto class
106	can round onto the wrong day; and multi-day courses are one event spanning first
107	start to last end, which is what makes `numberOfDays` and the daily window
108	derivable at all. That holds only because none of our courses use Corsizio's
109	`breakdownDates` for per-session hours.
110	
111	**A wrong price was being published to Google.** `structured-data.astro` had a
112	hardcoded price table listing CSD at 1195 when we charge 995/1095, and it
113	regex-parsed the free-text frontmatter date, falling back to _today_ whenever the
114	pattern missed, which published permanently-current events. Both are gone: real
115	ISO dates, and real prices as an `AggregateOffer` when personal and regular
116	registration differ. Courses with nothing scheduled now emit no Event markup at
117	all, which is correct, and their "None currently scheduled" button is rendered
118	from an empty list rather than being a placeholder row someone had to remember to
119	type.
120	
121	## 2026-08-04 — Quiz results: a shape instead of a balance bar, and the move stops going silent
122	
123	**Why.** The `map-move` results page led with a two-segment balance bar: the
124	proportion of gaining to slipping answers. It could say "this much of your time
125	was well spent" and nothing else, so it could not answer the question the page

Done. All six built, `astro check` and `lint:tw` clean, results page verified against four answer sets on a dev server.

## What changed

**`src/content/quizzes/scrum-master-ai/index.mdx`**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| step 3 | "Get one thing to **try**" | "Get one thing to **focus on**" |
| results H1 | "Here's what I see" | "Most of your recent Sprints went to **{box}**" (+ `headingFallback`) |
| `mostLine` | duplicated that sentence under the shape | removed |
| `opening` | "Just observations, and what I'd recommend…" | "…**Below: where your Sprints actually went, then the one change I'd make first.**" |
| shape tags | "less of this" / "more of this" | "take time from here" / "put it here" |
| `contextHeading` | "about your situation" | "the constraints you described" |
| q5 / q7 / q8 | 146 / 190 / 140 chars | 79 / 118 / 100 |
| `close` | "will not magically you or your team" | "will not magically **make** you…" |
| `slippingEmpty` | no full stop | fixed |

**Engine** — `mapMove.heading` now takes the same `{box}` substitution `mostLine` already had (`MapMoveResults.astro`, `schema.ts`, `types.ts`), plus `headingFallback` for when the heading wants a box and no shape was computed. README updated.

**`HISTORY.md`** — dated entry covering all six, plus what's still outstanding.

## Verified on a running dev server

- H1 interpolates correctly per answer set: "the mechanical work" (slipping-heavy), "the people work" (gaining), "the system work" (mixed)
- `the constraints you described` renders only when context answers exist
- Both move tags render; the move block still fires on context-heavy and mixed sets

One thing worth knowing about the long tag: `reclaimPriority` is q3/q1/q2, and every eligible answer in those three is `box: mechanical` — the full-width bottom row. So "take time from here" can only ever land on the wide box, and the short "put it here" is what lands on a half-width top-row box. No mobile overflow risk unless the priorities change.

Two notes:
- The README fails `prettier --check`, but it already did before this change. Running `--write` reflowed ~40 unrelated lines, so I reverted that and left the file as it was.
- q8's context answer ("I coach through the work as I go") now sits under "the constraints you described" and isn't a constraint. One option in thirty-two — flagged in `HISTORY.md`, not fixed.

Items 4 (role-conditional result copy) and 5 (pain-led hero kicker) untouched, as agreed.

`roleVariants` varies the copy that *wraps* the result by who the taker said
they are:

```yaml
mapMove:
  roleVariants:
    profileQuestion: role # id of the `profile` question that selects the variant
    variants:
      role-manager: # the `tag` on that question's chosen option
        opening: 'You answered for your Scrum Master, so…'
        close: '…'
        cta: { body: '…', buttonLabel: 'See the course', buttonHref: '/…/' }
```

Three things about it. **Variants are keyed by the option's existing `tag`**, the
same one the submission carries, so a role has one identifier rather than two
that drift apart. **A variant is a patch, not a copy**: fields it omits fall
through to the base, and a role with no entry at all just gets the base. And the
**overridable set is deliberately small** (`opening`, `close`, `cta`) — the
per-answer map and move sentences are already specific to what the taker chose,
so multiplying those by the number of roles buys little and costs a maintenance
multiplier on every future copy edit.

The `mapMove` block also holds the surrounding copy (`eyebrow`, `heading`,
`headingFallback`, `opening`, `shape`, column headings, `close`, `cta`, …) so the
engine stays free of site-specific wording.

```ts
import {

  type QuizResponses,

  type MapMoveShapeBox,
  type MapMoveShapeConfig,
} from '@/lib/quiz-engine';

import QuizStepper from '@/lib/quiz-engine/components/QuizStepper';
import ResultCard from '@/lib/quiz-engine/components/ResultCard.astro';
import MapMoveResults from '@/lib/quiz-engine/components/MapMoveResults.astro';
```

## Result styles

A quiz picks its results renderer with the `resultStyle` frontmatter field
(defaults to `'band'`):

- **`'band'`** — the total score maps to an overall level, and the results page
  renders the `<ResultCard section level>` blocks that match (everything above).
  Use for knowledge or risk quizzes with a "you scored X, you're a Y" result.
- **`'map-move'`** — no single band. Each answer is classified into a bucket, and
  the results page renders a two-column map (work getting more valuable vs. work
  slipping away) plus one recommended move. Use for reflective, per-answer
  quizzes.

The two styles share the same schema, stepper, and landing page; only the query
shape and the results renderer differ. The results page dispatches on
`resultStyle`.

68:**Profile questions.** A question with `kind: 'profile'` classifies the taker instead of assessing them: it is excluded from the score, from the map, and from the progress bar (so a cover promising "eight questions" stays honest), and it always leads regardless of `randomize`. Each of its options can carry a `tag` (applied to the submission as `tags[<name>]=true`, which is how the role reaches Cakemail) and a `lens` (a standing instruction shown from the moment that answer is picked and repeated above every later question). `scrum-master-ai` opens with one: Scrum Master / part-time Scrum Master / project manager / manager, tagged `role-*`. The manager option carries the `lens`, because every question after it says "you" and a manager would otherwise answer about their own week. Give a profile question a `section` id that is **not** one of the declared sections, or it adds a card to the landing page, and set `label` (the per-question eyebrow, which otherwise comes from the section) so it doesn't read as one of the questions the cover promised — `scrum-master-ai` uses "Before the eight questions", and the cover's how-it-works strip says the same thing. Like `levelTagPrefix`, `tag` collects nothing on a start gate, since nothing is answered at submit time. Plain "team member" is deliberately not an option: q7 and q8 would score a team member's correct answers as gaps.
70:**Audience and segmentation.** Quiz signups go to the general `Newsletter Subscribers` list (the same list as post-course and general signups). The current `scrum-master-ai` quiz tags submissions `sm-role-ai` (via `submissionTags`) plus a `role-*` tag from the profile question, so a future nurture sequence can trigger on either; Cakemail auto-creates the tag on first submission and lowercases it (see [[reference-cakemail-lowercase-tags]]). The quiz's capture copy tells users up front that they're subscribing to the list, so one list per consent is correct and the tag is the segmentation. The engine also supports a per-tier tag via the `levelTagPrefix` frontmatter field (for `map-move`, the tier is the framing bucket), but `scrum-master-ai` does not set it. The tag rides along in the same submission (`tags[sm-role-ai]=true`), forwarded by `/api/newsletter-signup` to the consolidated Cakemail form, so no dedicated quiz form is needed. (The retired `ai-failure-modes` quiz used the `aiquiz` tag; the two AI lead-magnet download forms still apply `aiquiz` — see "General newsletter signup" below.)

Plain "team member" is deliberately not an option: q7 and q8 would score a team member's correct answers as gaps.

**The role also changes the results copy** (`mapMove.roleVariants`). Variants are keyed by the **same `tag`** the option already carries, so a role has one identifier rather than two that drift; `profileQuestion` names the question that selects one. A variant is a patch, not a copy — fields it omits fall through to the base, and a role with no entry gets the base unchanged (which is why `scrum-master-ai` has no `role-scrum-master` entry). Only `opening`, `close` and `cta` are overridable, deliberately: the per-answer map and move sentences are already specific to what the taker chose, so multiplying those by four roles would buy little and impose a 4× cost on every future copy edit. `resolveMapMoveCopy()` does the merge; the results page never reads `quiz.mapMove` raw.

content.content: 62:**Capture position.** The `capturePosition` frontmatter field (`'start' | 'end'`, default `'end'`) decides where the email step sits. `scrum-master-ai` uses `'end'`: the email is asked for after the last question, and the capture form's own button is what finishes the quiz. Flow: cover (hero + "Start the quiz" button + 3-step "how it works" strip) with the "Before you start" card sitting underneath as step 0 of the stepper → 8 questions → capture card (first name optional + email) → results. **The cover states the ask up front** — `heroButtonNote` under the start button and a closing line in `intro` both say the email comes after the last question — so nobody meets the form as a surprise. The cover's marketing chrome hides on step index ≠ 0, not on step kind, because which step is first depends on the capture position. Capture wording is per-quiz frontmatter (`captureHeading`, `captureBody`, `captureButtonLabel`, `captureFootnote`), as is the hero's small print (`heroButtonNote`); `captureButtonLabel` is deliberately unset here so the button falls back to `submitButtonLabel` ("Show me my map"), which is what it actually does.

Two rules: **colour encodes meaning, never decoration** (four roles: valuable / slipping / context / accent-recommendation, always backed by an icon + label + position, and slipping is amber rather than red because red reads as failure), and **flat surfaces** (white cards with hairline borders, tinted panels with none, no gradients or shadows, the one exception being the 2px accent border on the "one move" callout). Serif headings over sans body, weights 400/500 only, sentence case, ~680px column. The palette lives as `--color-quiz-*` tokens in `src/styles/global.css` so restyling means redefining tokens, not editing components; the accent is APR brand blue. **Icons are named by concept** (`icon: 'admin'`) and resolved in `src/lib/quiz-engine/components/QuizIcon.tsx`, the only file that knows the icon family. Currently Lucide; Mark has a one-month Streamline subscription and intends to swap in Streamline icons + cover illustrations, which is a one-file change with no frontmatter edits.

## 2026-08-05 — The role now changes the result, and the hero leads with the reason

**Why.** These were the two items left from the 29 July critique, both held back
because they needed copy rather than plumbing. The point of both is the same one
the critique kept returning to: the page should speak to the person in front of
it, not to the category of person.

**`mapMove.roleVariants`.** The role question has been collected since 30 July
and did nothing on the results page: the tag went to Cakemail and the manager
option carried a `lens` for the questions, and that was all. Variants are keyed
by **the option's existing `tag`**, not a new identifier, so the role has one
name across the submission and the results page and they cannot drift apart. A
variant is a patch: fields it omits fall through, so `role-scrum-master` has no
entry at all, because the base copy was already written for them.

**Only `opening`, `close` and `cta` are overridable**, which is the argument
worth keeping. The critique proposed roles × result buckets, a matrix of
customised result text. But the per-answer map and move sentences are *already*
specific to what the taker chose, which is where nearly all of the "this is about
me" effect actually comes from; multiplying them by four roles would have added
little and put a 4× cost on every future copy edit, paid by one person. The three
fields that do vary are the ones that frame the result, and the manager's `cta`
is the one with a direct revenue argument: a manager should not be sold the same
line as a part-time Scrum Master.

The manager variant also does a job nothing else could. Every sentence on the
page says "you", and a manager answered for someone else, so the opening now says
so out loud: read it as them, the way you answered. That is the honest fix; the
alternative was a second set of third-person map sentences, i.e. exactly the
matrix just rejected.

**`heroKicker`.** The critique's strongest single claim was that leading with the
fear ("are you a Scrum Master worried the role disappears?") would triple
conversion. The headline had already been rewritten on 30 July in a different
direction, for reasons that still hold, so this takes both: the kicker carries
**why the reader is here** and the heading carries **what they get**. Splitting
those two jobs is what makes the addition free rather than a trade. It is an APR
field in `content.config.ts`, not an engine one, since it is landing-page
marketing rather than quiz mechanics. `heroBody` also picked up the second half
of the critique's line, that the quiz says how much of your week is already work
a tool could take.

**One thing not done.** The banner, modal and sidebar in `cta.ts` still carry the
headline verbatim and no kicker. That is correct for now: the kicker answers "why
am I on this page", which those three surfaces answer by being where they are.

content.text:
Both built. `astro check` clean (0/0/0), `lint:tw` clean, verified on a dev server across all four roles.

## Item 5 — pain-led hero kicker

New APR field `heroKicker` (`content.config.ts`, rendered above the `h1` in `[slug].astro`):

> **For Scrum Masters wondering whether the role survives this.**
> Which parts of the Scrum Master job still need a person?

The split is the point: the kicker carries **why the reader is here**, the heading carries **what they get**. That takes Mike's fear-lead without discarding the 30 July headline decision. `heroBody` also picked up the second half of his line ("how much of your week is already work a tool could take"). The banner/modal/sidebar in `cta.ts` are unchanged — they answer "why am I here" by being where they are.

Styling is `text-base font-medium` in accent blue. The results-page eyebrow is `text-sm`; I went a size up because this is a sentence rather than a label, but say the word and it drops.

## Item 4 — `mapMove.roleVariants`

```yaml
roleVariants:
  profileQuestion: role
  variants:
    role-part-time-sm:    { opening, close }
    role-project-manager: { opening, close }
    role-manager:         { opening, close, cta }
```

- Keyed by the option's **existing `tag`** — one identifier per role across the submission and the results page, so they can't drift.
- A variant is a **patch**: omitted fields fall through. `role-scrum-master` has no entry because the base copy was already written for them.
- Only `opening`, `close`, `cta` are overridable. Your call was the right one to hold: the per-answer map and move sentences are already specific to what they chose, so a roles × buckets matrix would have added little and put a 4× cost on every future copy edit.

New engine export `resolveMapMoveCopy()` in `map-move.ts` does the merge; `MapMoveResults.astro` no longer reads `quiz.mapMove` raw.

**Verified:** each role gets its own `opening` with no bleed between them, the manager gets "Want your Scrum Masters ready for this?" and the other three keep the base CTA.

The manager variant does one thing nothing else could — every sentence on the page says "you" and a manager answered for someone else, so the opening now says so: *"Everything below says 'you': read it as them."* The alternative was a second set of third-person map sentences, which is the matrix we just declined.

## What needs your pen

**The six new copy blocks are my draft, not your voice.** Particularly:
- the manager `close`, which argues "the mechanical half gets cheap, so the coaching half becomes the whole of the value" — that's a positioning claim you may want to make differently
- the part-time `close`, which promises AI hands hours back; softer or harder is a judgement call

Docs updated: `CLAUDE.md` (both features), `HISTORY.md` (new entry), engine `README.md`.

Note `CLAUDE.md` fails `prettier --check`, as it did before this change — I left it rather than reflow the whole file into the diff.
I tightened all three of the openings. Please check my use of English.

content.text:
One real error, three nits.

## Error: comma splice (project manager)

> The questions were about the behaviours, not the job title**,** the opportunities to help are there for anyone.

Two independent clauses joined by a comma. Also two smaller things in the same sentence: "the behaviours" takes a definite article with nothing to refer back to, and it's plural against a singular "the job title".

Options:
- **"The questions were about behaviours, not job titles: the opportunity to help is there for anyone."** — the colon does the work the comma can't, and signals that the second half explains the first
- "The questions were about behaviours, not job titles, so the opportunity to help is there for anyone."

## Nits

**"buy back"** (part-time close) — *"What it can do is buy back some of the hours the admin takes."* GenAI doesn't buy anything; it's not a transaction. "win back", "claw back" or "give you back" all land the same idea without the purchase metaphor.

**"those Sprints"** (part-time opening) — *"Below: where those Sprints went"*. The antecedent is loose: the preceding sentence talks about hours and time, not Sprints. "where those hours went" both fixes the reference and reinforces the hours framing you set up in the first clause.

**"below" twice** (manager opening) — *"Everything **below** says 'you'… **Below**: where the time went"*. Two different senses a sentence apart. "Everything that follows says 'you'" clears it.

## Fine as written

- **"behaviours"** — consistent with the site: 116 uses of the -our spelling in `src/content` against 35 of -or
- **"read it as them"** — momentarily ambiguous but idiomatic, and the alternative ("read it as your Scrum Master") is clumsier
- **"Want your team learning to adapt?"** — grammatical; *want* takes an object plus a present participle
- Both other openings are clean, and all three read tighter than my drafts

Want me to apply the comma-splice fix and the three nits?

**One thing not done.** The banner, modal and sidebar in `cta.ts` still carry the

## 2026-08-05 — The map columns stop stretching to each other

**Why.** The two map columns were grid items, so they inherited `align-items:
stretch`. A taker with four slipping answers and no gaining ones got a bordered
card containing one line of "not much showed up here" drawn the full height of
the four findings beside it: about 500px of empty box, which reads as something
that failed to load rather than as an answer.

**What it does now.** When either column is empty the two stack full width, and
`md:items-start` handles the milder case where both have content but unequal
amounts. Stacking is the better fix rather than merely un-stretching, because it
also widens the surviving list from a ~35-character measure to the full column;
side by side, four findings wrapped every five words. Nothing that carries
meaning depends on the two being adjacent: each card still has its own icon,
label and colour, and when one side is empty there is no comparison to draw
anyway.

**The two columns became one loop while it was open.** They had been
copy-pasted, identical but for the bucket, heading, icon and colour, which is why
the empty-state markup had already drifted apart in whitespace between them.

content.text:
Fixed in `MapMoveResults.astro`.

## What was happening

The two columns were grid items, so they inherited `align-items: stretch` — the empty card was drawn to match the height of the four findings beside it. That's the ~500px void in your screenshot.

## What it does now

**Either column empty → the two stack full width.** Un-stretching alone would have left the same void, just unbordered. Stacking also fixes the second problem in that screenshot: side by side, the four slipping findings wrap every five words at a ~35-character measure. Full width they get the whole column.

**Both populated → `md:items-start`**, so each card sizes to its own content instead of the shorter one padding out to match.

Verified across four cases:

| | layout |
|---|---|
| gaining empty, 4 slipping | stacked |
| slipping empty, all gaining | stacked |
| both populated | 2-col, `items-start` |
| both empty (all mixed) | stacked |

Nothing meaning-bearing depends on the two being adjacent — each card keeps its own icon, label and colour, and when one side is empty there's no comparison to draw.

The two column blocks were also copy-paste duplicates (identical but for bucket, heading, icon and colour, and their empty-state markup had already drifted apart in whitespace). They're now one `columns.map()`.

`astro check` 0/0/0, `lint:tw` clean, prettier clean. `HISTORY.md` entry added.
Is there some reason not to stack it everytime?

No, not really. I made it conditional out of caution and the caution doesn't hold up:

- **The length cost is smaller than it looks.** Side by side the measure is ~45 characters, so a 130-character finding takes 3 lines; full width it takes 2. Stacking four findings plus three costs roughly 75px net, not the screenful I assumed. It doesn't meaningfully push "where I'd start" down.
- **The columns were never really doing the comparison.** You can't scan two lists of 2-3 line prose sentences against each other. The at-a-glance contrast is the shape's job, and the shape does it. The columns are detail, and detail wants measure.
- **Mobile is already stacked**, so the conditional means the layout you see when checking on a phone isn't the layout most desktop takers get.

The only thing lost is that "appreciating" and "depreciating" stop being physically opposite. The headings, icons and colour still say it.
